item.title: Five Extinct Sharks Once Swam Where Egypt’s Desert Stands Today
item.description: Today, the Abu Tartur Plateau in Egypt is a dry, rugged desert. Around 80 million years ago, however, this same landscape lay beneath a productive tropical sea. Fourteen fossilized teeth belonging to five extinct shark species are helping paleontologists reconstruct that vanished ecosystem, revealing how multiple predators could share the same waters by occupying different ecological niches.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Cristina Márquez, Contributor
